issues.title: Obtain the county's 2026 appropriation ordinance
issues.detail: Found on clarkcountyar.gov and the state transparency portal. Ingested; it is the money trail tree.

stamped.revealed: The county appropriates $21,386,230 across roughly 40 funds for 2026. The sheriff and jail lines are 40.9% of the General Fund ($2,795,178 of $6,829,201); adding emergency management (OEM) makes it 43.1%. 9-1-1 is a separate fund. The tree above is this ordinance, made navigable.

issues.title: City of Arkadelphia budget
issues.detail: The city budget document is not posted online. It can be requested from city hall.

stamped.revealed: The city's audited financials are online; its budget document is not. FY2022, FY2023, and FY2024 city audits plus the FY2023 water & sewer system audit are now stored in the document library. FY2024 (regulatory basis): general fund revenues $18.2M, expenditures $13.2M, year-end balance $2.3M.

research_notes: What the internet answers: audited actuals (layer two) for the city, 2022–2024, via Arkansas Legislative Audit.
What it cannot answer: the budget document itself — line items, department detail, city salaries. That remains a records request at city hall.

issues.title: School district budgets & millage breakdown
issues.detail: Arkadelphia Public Schools + Gurdon. District offices and state education records.

stamped.revealed: School millage is now sourced: inside Arkadelphia city limits, school mills are 47.65 of 59.75 total mills (State Millage Report 2025, p.15). Arkadelphia 47.65 mills (25.0 M&O + 2.0 other M&O + 17.65 bond + 3.0 other bond), Gurdon 43.0. Both districts' FY2024 audits are stored, and the Arkadelphia district's bond official statements show how it borrows. Voters approved a 17.65-mill debt tax at the 2015 school election. That tax repays 2015 bonds that built a new middle and elementary school, 2021 bonds ($20.035M) that refinanced them at a lower rate, and 2022 bonds ($15.015M) that built a new elementary school, finished in 2024, using spare room in the same tax with no new vote. The 2021 and 2022 bonds total $35.05M, with $43.3M in principal and interest left at mid-2024, repaid through May 2047. Separately, voters on November 18, 2025 approved 3 more mills (44.65 to 47.65, about $60 a year on a $100,000 home) and $37.17M in bonds for a new high school, due July 2028. The district's bond records go back to 2003, with issues overlapping ever since.

research_notes: What the internet answers: audited district financials (Arkansas Legislative Audit), millage with full M&O/bond breakdown (DESE + state millage books), statewide comparison data (MySchoolInfo).
What it cannot answer yet: the districts' own budget documents with line-item detail. Arkadelphia posts state-required financial documents at arkadelphiaschools.org; pulling them is the next step.

Bond sources (read 2026-09-26): official statements on EMMA for the 2012 ($635K construction), 2015 ($21.195M refunding and construction), 2021 ($20.035M refunding), 2022 ($15.015M construction), and 2026 ($37.17M construction) issues, plus the University of Arkansas voter fact sheet for the 2025 election, all in the document library. The 2021 statement says those bonds refund the 2015 bonds; the 2022 statement says no tax was voted for them and they rest on surplus from existing debt taxes. The FY2024 audit (Notes 5–6, pp. 16–18) confirms the 2021/2022 totals and the elementary school contract.
Still open: certified vote totals for the 2015 and 2025 school elections (county canvass), and whether the elementary work funded in 2015 and the elementary school funded in 2022 are the same campus.
Fringe complication mapped: parts of Clark County are in Bismarck, Centerpoint, Delight, and Harmony Grove districts — tax bills differ by where in the county you live.

issues.title: Millage rate sheet & sales tax inventory
issues.detail: The revenue side of the whole tree: every mill, every dedicated sales tax, what each costs a $100,000 home.

stamped.revealed: The millage half is answered from the state's own millage books (2024 and 2025 editions stored). County 7.1 mills — including road 3.0, library 1.0, hospital 1.0, and college 1.0 — plus city mills (Arkadelphia 5.0, Gurdon 5.4) and school mills (43.0–47.65). Total in Arkadelphia city limits: 59.75 mills ≈ $1,195/year on a $100,000 home before the homestead credit. The sales-tax half is now partly answered from the county's state audits: the EDCCC tax is a countywide half-cent approved by voters June 12, 2007 and renewed March 11, 2014 and June 8, 2021, seven years each, all remitted to EDCCC. A 0.5% sales tax pledge repays the county's $8.46M 2021 road bonds (Truck Bypass), 1.125–2.00% interest, through June 2036.

research_notes: Sales-tax detail from the audits: the road-bond fund took in $469,373 (2022) and $678,806 (2023) in sales taxes against debt payments of $341,005 and $670,756; the audits say any excess may be used for any lawful purpose. $1,249,445 in interest over the bonds' life at issue.

Still open: the enacting ordinances' exact ballot wording and vote totals (County Clerk), the fire sales tax's rate and terms, and the FY2024 county audit (not yet published). The ordinances live in the county's online ordinance archive (see Docket #9's portal).
Small ambiguity, labeled on the millage line: the exact mapping of the county's general/misc mills between city and rural residents needs a visual check of the millage book's table layout.

issues.title: The complete fire funding map
issues.detail: District budgets + dues + millage + city FD + the county's $45,921 pass-through.

stamped.revealed: The structure is mapped: Clark County levies no fire millage (confirmed in the state millage book), so rural departments run on dues, donations, and the county's $45,921 pass-through, while the Arkadelphia FD is funded inside the city budget (whose audits are now stored). Departments identified: Arkadelphia FD, East Clark County Rural VFD, Okolona VFD, Whelen Springs VFD, and the Clark County Fire Association (501(c)(3), postcard filer — no public financials).

research_notes: What the internet answers: the funding architecture, the department roster, and the fact that no fire millage exists here.
What it cannot answer: each department's dues schedule, membership counts, and finances — postcard 990s publish nothing. Those details are not in any document we hold.
The county's $45,921 pass-through is one of several fire-funding sources (see /line/fire-passthrough).

issues.title: EDCCC incentives — who receives the $1.84M?
issues.detail: Recipient list, agreements, performance terms. EDCCC records and quorum court minutes; FOIA if needed.

stamped.revealed: No online source we found names the recipients. EDCCC does not appear in the IRS exempt-organization file, so there are no public 990s. It is administered through the Arkadelphia Alliance, a separate 501(c)(6) that files 990s showing about $800K a year of its own revenue. The recipient trail runs through EDCCC board minutes and quorum court minutes — offline or in the county's document portal.

research_notes: Entity map: EDCCC (owns the 991-acre Southwest Arkansas Mega Site; 15-member board; a paid chief executive) · Arkadelphia Regional Economic Development Alliance, 501(c)(6), EIN 26-2859118 (administers; 990s on ProPublica) · Clark County Industrial Council, 501(c)(6), EIN 58-1763488 (postcard filer).

The tax is a voter-approved half-cent county sales tax. Fund 3407 appropriations across stored budgets: $1,960,273 (2022) → $1,872,787 (2025) → $1,844,538 (2026). The appropriation has declined across these years; the documents do not state a reason.

Governance documented in the OCR'd minutes: the county judge nominates and the quorum court approves EDCCC board members (appointment votes recorded December 2024, 11-0, and in 2026, 9-0); the CEO delivers quarterly reports to the court. The board has 15 members and meets six times a year at noon at Fairfield Inn & Suites, Arkadelphia. The Alliance publishes the board roster at arkadelphiaalliance.com.

State site-development grants to EDCCC: $1,013,710 (December 2024) and $3,792,543 (April 2026) for the industrial site near Gum Springs (news report: [The Arkadelphian, April 29, 2026](https://arkadelphian.com/2026/04/29/edccc-among-22-set-to-receive-state-funding-for-industrial-site-development/)). Contracts with recipients would be in EDCCC's own records, which is what a records request is for.
Lifetime collections are now sourced: $25,431,732 from 2008 through 2023, from the county's state audits (each year's figure is cited on its audit in the document library).

Next step: the minutes show the EDCCC CEO gives the quorum court quarterly reports with handouts and slides. Request the last 8 quarterly reports from the county clerk, then the enacting ordinance from the county archive, then the incentive agreements.

issues.title: Neighboring county salary schedules
issues.detail: Garland, Hot Spring, Nevada, Pike, Ouachita — same ordinance type, same public availability. The deputy salary comparison table.

stamped.revealed: The side-by-side table is live at /compare/deputy-pay, built from each county's own filed documents. Garland County's 2026 filing lists patrol deputies at $57,418–$58,540 (65 positions); Clark's 2026 schedule lists $43,398–$46,498. Garland's 2024 salary survey listed about $42,770. Nevada pays $32,400 flat; Pike's 2024 figure was $43,202. Ouachita pools deputies into one line (not per-deputy comparable); Hot Spring's filings are scans awaiting OCR.

research_notes: Remaining: an OCR pass on the Hot Spring and Pike 2026 filings (stored as image-only scans), which would complete all five neighbors at 2026 rates.

New (2026-07-18): the county's own base-pay ordinances (2016–2025, all stored and OCR'd) show deputy starting pay rose 32% in four years — $32,898 in 2022 to $43,398 in 2026. Clark starting deputy pay by ordinance: $32,898 (2022), $34,398 (2023), $41,398 (2025), $43,398 (2026). Two deputy slots were pending applicants when Ordinance 2025-22 passed.

issues.title: Remaining line-item pages of the county ordinance
issues.detail: Sheriff, Jail, Assessor, District Court, Prosecutor, Juvenile, OEM, Coroner, Health, Circuit Judge, Extension, Veterans — plus the ~20 smaller special funds and page-level references for every number already ingested. The pages exist in the filed document; finish the ingestion.

stamped.revealed: The 96-page budget packet is stored and page-pinning has begun: 29 amounts now cite their exact page, applied only after an automated keyword check against the page text. 70 more amounts appear on multiple pages and await one-by-one review; the department line-item pages themselves are the next ingestion push.

issues.title: Legislative audit reports & treasurer's reports
issues.detail: arklegaudit.gov. Layer two of the money trail: what was actually spent vs. appropriated, findings, and fund restrictions on the ~$3.9M in unappropriated balances.

stamped.revealed: County audits for FY2021, FY2022, and FY2023 are stored (FY2024 not yet published by the state), and the findings sections are now published at /audits: the auditors reported no material weaknesses and no reportable noncompliance for the county (FY2023), the city (FY2022–24), the water system, or either school district — quoted and cited.

research_notes: Treasurer's monthly/annual reports are not online — county records request.
FY2023 audit context found in the state's summary: the county's short-term financing debt limit was $8.65M at the end of 2023.

issues.title: Quorum court minutes & 2026 amendments
issues.detail: Ordinance amendments change this tree mid-year. Minutes feed outcome tracking.

stamped.revealed: Archived: all 38 quorum court minutes documents for 2024–2026 (regular sessions, budget committee, personnel committee, special sessions) pulled from the county's document portal into inbox/minutes/ — including the budget committee meetings that wrote the 2026 budget. They are scanned images without a text layer, so an OCR pass is queued before they can be searched and ingested.

research_notes: OCR complete (2026-07-18): 35 of 38 minutes now machine-readable after fixing a scan-decoding bug (1-bit images sheared by row padding; pipeline/lib-ocr.js corrects it). 3 files failed to download from the portal.

What the readable minutes document: the 2025–26 ambulance contract sequence (RFQs from Valor and Pafford → public comment with both owners speaking → Valor awarded → contract stalls in review → Valor closes, staff move to Pafford → county pivots to a Pafford contract), EDCCC quarterly reports delivered to the court by its chief executive, EDCCC board appointments made by the court, county property purchases, and every budget-season vote.

Equally important — what is NOT in the minutes: no asphalt, fuel, or gravel bid awards appear in any quorum court session. Commodity purchasing runs through the county judge's office, which means the check register (Docket #10) is the route we have identified to those vendor names.
The quorum court meets the second Monday of each month — now in the platform's calendar config.

October 12, 2026 regular session agenda (posted publicly by the county clerk's office on Oct. 6): the EDCCC 2026 third-quarter report; Proposed Ordinance 2026-11, “An ordinance to promote transparency and online access to Clark County Quorum Court records”; the quarterly ambulance report; a proposed appropriation ordinance and a proposed resolution, both to be set after the Oct. 7 budget committee meeting; and disposal of county property (a rail car bridge). The agenda lists the meeting at the Clark County Court Complex Building, 419 Clay St — not the 401 Clay St courtroom named in earlier minutes. Confirm the room with the clerk before you go.

issues.title: The hospital and college mills — 1 mill each, countywide (about $346,000 a year each, estimated)
issues.detail: The state millage book lists 1 mill each, countywide, for the hospital and the college (State Millage Report 2025, p.15). At an estimated $346M assessed value, derived from the [FY2023 county audit](/documents#clark-legaudit-2023) debt-limit figure, 1 mill is about $346,000 a year. Neither levy appears in the county appropriation ordinance. The documents we hold do not name the receiving entities or their reporting.
research_notes: The estimate is derived, not transcribed: 2.5% of assessed value = $8,652,005 legal debt limit ([FY2023 county audit](/documents#clark-legaudit-2023), debt-limit page) → assessed value ≈ $346M → 1 mill ≈ $346K/year. Actual collections will differ; the county tax settlement and treasurer's reports carry the real figures.

First document to pull: Ordinance 2025-19, the annual tax levy ordinance adopted December 8, 2025 (in the county's online ordinance archive) — its text should state the hospital and college levies and their statutory basis.
Then: which hospital entity and which college receive the proceeds, and what public reporting each provides. The same two questions apply to the EDCCC fund (Docket #5).
Both levies are listed in the state millage book (State Millage Report 2025, p.15). The vote or statute that established each is not yet in the corpus.

issues.title: County check register (layer three)
issues.detail: Which vendor got which check. Public under Arkansas FOIA; not currently posted online.

stamped.revealed: The 'Who gets paid' page is live at /vendors with every payee a public document has named so far — Pioneer Civil Construction ($1.58M landfill closure), Total Assessment Solutions ($825,840 reappraisal), Southern Bancorp (county's lender), the 2021 road-bond holders ($8.46M principal, ~$1.08M interest through 2036, repaid by a pledged 0.5% sales tax), and the Valor→Pafford ambulance contract (quorum court minutes). The asphalt, fuel, and gravel suppliers remain unnamed in any posted document — and the page now carries a ready-to-send Arkansas FOIA request for the check register and bid tabulations.

research_notes: The audits also surfaced a reverse trail: gas and oil companies reimbursed the county's road fund $715,948 in 2023.
Sending the FOIA letter is a human step — any Arkansas citizen can; the template is on the /vendors page.

issues.detail: The share of treated water that leaks or goes unbilled isn’t published.

issues.title: The water plant’s capacity and age
issues.detail: How many million gallons a day the treatment plant can make, how much it makes now, and when it was built and last upgraded — the basics for planning growth.

issues.title: Arkadelphia’s PFAS test results
issues.detail: EPA’s national sampling (UCMR 5) tested for “forever chemicals.” Arkadelphia’s results weren’t findable. Next step: EPA’s UCMR data or ask the utility.

issues.title: The lead service line inventory
issues.detail: Every system had to list its lead and galvanized service lines by Oct 2024. Arkadelphia’s inventory hasn’t been found published. Next step: ask the utility.

issues.title: Water and sewer rates
issues.detail: The current water and sewer rate schedule isn’t posted in a source we hold.

issues.title: The new jail: cost, size, and design
issues.detail: The sheriff has called for a new jail at least double the current capacity ([The Arkadelphian, May 12, 2026](https://arkadelphian.com/2026/05/12/sheriff-watson-its-time-to-get-serious-about-the-future-of-housing-prisoners/)). Its cost, site, financing and design haven’t been announced.

issues.title: Programs inside the Clark County jail
issues.detail: Whether the jail offers any garden, GED, trade, recovery, or reentry program — none was found documented.

issues.title: Where the pandemic relief money went
issues.detail: Clark County received federal ARPA funds, and the 2026 budget still carries $471,142 of it. The total received and a full list of what it paid for aren’t documented here yet. Next step: the U.S. Treasury’s allocation list and the county’s ARPA reports.

issues.title: Ordinance 2026-11 — online access to quorum court records
issues.detail: On the Oct. 12, 2026 agenda: a proposed ordinance “to promote transparency and online access to Clark County Quorum Court records.” Its text isn’t posted yet. Next step: get the text from the county clerk and file it here. If the court adopts it, this item tracks what it requires — which records, how soon, for how long — and whether each part gets done.

issues.title: Money filings for every county candidate and officeholder
issues.detail: Arkansas requires each county officeholder and candidate to file a Statement of Financial Interest every year, and each candidate to file campaign contribution and expenditure reports. Next step: request all of them from the county clerk (or the Secretary of State, if Act 524 of 2025 moved the campaign reports there) — both county judge candidates, every quorum court candidate, and every sitting elected official — and post each one as filed, in the same format for everyone.
